pois.name: Akihabara Station
pois.description: The beating heart of Tokyo's electronics and anime culture. The station's 'Electric Town' exit opens onto a district where neon signs compete for attention and every building houses multiple floors of gadgets, games, and manga.

pois.name: Animate Akihabara
pois.description: Japan's largest anime, manga, and game retailer — 8 floors of character goods, manga volumes, Blu-rays, and otaku merchandise. The flagship store draws thousands daily, with themed floors rotating by franchise season.

pois.name: Yodobashi Camera Akiba
pois.description: Tokyo's largest electronics megastore — 9 floors of cameras, computers, appliances, and games with tax-free shopping for tourists. The rooftop has a camera test course and the basement a gourmet food hall.

pois.name: Super Potato Retro Game Store
pois.description: A legendary retro game store spanning 3 floors — Famicom, Super Famicom, Mega Drive, and PlayStation classics in their original boxes. The second floor is a playable museum where you can test vintage consoles. A pilgrimage site for gaming historians.

pois.name: Akihabara Cultural Zone
pois.description: The pedestrian-only 'Chuo-dori' street on weekends transforms into a pedestrian paradise lined with maid cafes, idol venues, and pop-up events. The epicentre of Japan's otaku culture since the 1980s.
